evals.prompt: Design the permissions and UI/backend authorization model for a new admin users module. We need list, detail, sensitive data, create user, update profile, change status, assign role, reset password, archive, and delete.
evals.expected_output: A permission-first RBAC design with explicit names, separated route and action access, backend endpoint mapping, and field-level authorization guidance.
expectations: Uses explicit permission names like users.list, users.read.basic, and users.update.status
Separates route access from in-page action access
Keeps backend authorization as the final authority
Mentions field-level authorization for partial updates

evals.prompt: Our support agents can see the user list and change account status, but they must not open the full user detail page. Propose the correct UI and permission model.
evals.expected_output: A minimum-action UI design that keeps the list page, blocks the detail page, and exposes only a narrow status-edit interaction backed by a dedicated permission and endpoint.
expectations: Avoids rendering a full detail page for update-without-read access
Uses a narrow UI such as a modal, drawer, or inline editor
Models the update as users.update.status or an equivalent explicit permission
Preserves separate route and action permission checks

evals.prompt: Review this authorization design: we have users.read, users.update, and one PATCH /users/:id endpoint that updates any field. Rewrite it into a safer permission model.
evals.expected_output: A critique of the broad permission model plus a replacement design with split read permissions, split update permissions, dedicated endpoints, and payload-level authorization rules.
expectations: Flags broad permissions such as users.read or users.update as insufficient
Introduces split read or update permissions
States that unauthorized payload fields should be rejected or blocked
